messages:
Infra Bot: :rotating_light: Alert — spike in 5xx and TLS handshake errors to api.redwood.ai from multiple regions (NA/EU/APAC). Detected by edge-health monitor.
Alex M.: Confirming, seeing a lot of `tls: handshake failure` in gateway logs + Cloudflare edge connection resets. 5xx rate up 8x in last 3m.
Jamie (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SRE lead and infra. Priorities: 1) mitigate customer impact, 2) gather scope, 3) contact Cloudflare.
Priya K.: Quick hit list — are we seeing DNS failures or just TLS?
Alex M.: Mostly TLS handshake failures and `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` from certain Cloudflare POPlist. DNS lookups succeed. Traces show Cloudflare dropping to origin or resetting early.
Support: Customer reports incoming: a handful of customers seeing timeouts and failed API calls. CS triage page: https://redwood.internal/cs/incidents/2519001234 (link).
SRE Lead: Runbook step 1: confirm scope, step 2: fail traffic to alternate POPs or disable HTTP/2 early hints if CF misnegotiating. Jamie, can you run the curl checks from multiple regions?
Jamie (oncall): Running checks now from eu-west, us-east, ap-southeast.
Jamie (oncall): eu-west: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health` -> TLS handshake fail. us-east: GET succeeds but with elevated latency (450ms). ap-southeast: handshake fail.
Alex M.: Interesting — suggests partial POP-level degradation. Cloudflare dashboard shows elevated errors from specific PoPs in EU & APAC.
Cloudflare Support Bot: We are investigating an edge routing issue affecting TLS handshakes in some POPs. See https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/edge-routing/ (internal status link).
Priya K.: Mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily toggle Cloudflare `always_online`/`http2`? 2) increase origin connection limits? 3) apply a quick Worker to route traffic away from problematic POPs via `colo` header? Which is fastest?
SRE Lead: Fastest is to add a Worker that appends `CF-Pop: bypass` header? We don't have a reliable mapping. Better: update load-balancer steering to prefer healthy regions + increase client-side retry/backoff.
Alex M.: We can push a short-lived downgrade: force TLS 1.2 cipher-suite (if CF negotiation mismatches) via origin config? That requires infra change, takes longer.
Jamie (oncall): I can update API gateway to add a retry-layer on the public SDK proxies: increase retries to 3 and exponential backoff. That should reduce customer-visible errors while we wait on Cloudflare. Pushing in 2m.
Support: Notifying customers in affected SLA tier now. Message draft posted to incident channel: "We are experiencing intermittent API failures; mitigation in progress; more updates shortly." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Infra Bot: Automated runbook lookup -> runbook `cdn-tls-handshake` matches symptoms. Recommended temporary action: set `edge_fallback` to origin via `load-balancer` for affected hostnames.
Alex M.: I'll prepare LB change to prefer direct origin path (bypass CF cache) for a subset of traffic — aim for <5% initially. This reduces CF in-path but increases origin load.
SRE Lead: Set canary to 5% traffic reroute. Monitor origin CPU and request latency. Observability Bot, throw up dashboards for origin CPU, 5xx, and CF edge errors.
Observability Bot: Dashboards live: https://app.datadog.com/dash/edge-tls-2519001234 (internal). Origin CPU baseline is 28% — estimated safe for +5% traffic.
Jamie (oncall): Rolling LB change now: `traffic_split: cf=95 origin=5`.
Alex M.: Change applied. Watch metrics.
Priya K.: Early signal: 5xx rate down 30% for affected customers routed to origin. Some customers still seeing retries fail (those pinned to specific POPs).
Cloudflare Support Bot: Root cause identified: routing flap between two backbone peers causing TLS session renegotiation failures in subset of colos. Working on diff/rollback.
SRE Lead: Good. Next steps: 1) keep partial origin reroute, 2) increase client SDK retry w/ jitter, 3) coordinate with Cloudflare for rollback window, 4) prepare customer status update.
Support: Updated customer message: "Mitigation in place — we have rerouted a portion of traffic to our origin which has reduced errors for many customers. Cloudflare reports ongoing remediation on their edge routing. We'll post another update in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:
Jamie (oncall): Patching SDK proxy now: adding `max_retries=3, backoff=200ms`. Deployed to edge proxies in 1m.
Alex M.: Also placing a temporary NGINX config on origin to accept TLS 1.2+1.3 and increase keepalive time to reduce renegotiations. Deploying as precaution.
SRE Lead: Good. Logging: capture full `ClientHello` rejection samples and upload to incident artifacts: `s3://redwood-incidents/2519001234/clienthellos/`. Alex, mark when done.
Alex M.: Uploaded sample bundles and packet captures. Link: https://s3.redwood/internal/2519001234/clienthellos.tar.gz (internal).
Cloudflare Support Bot: We have implemented a routing rollback in the affected POPlist. Propagation ~ 3-7m. Monitoring metrics now.
Observability Bot: Edge handshake errors trending down across most colos. Global 5xx normalized to ~close-to-baseline but small spikes persist in APAC.
Priya K.: Can we quantify impacted customers and error budget burn? Support, do we have list?
Support: We have 18 active customers with error rates >5%. 4 are enterprise with SLA implications. Contacted account owners.
SRE Lead: Action items and owners: Jamie — monitor retries and errors, Priya — coordinate Cloudflare comms + postmortem lead, Alex — artifact collection and origin config rollback plan, Support — customer comms and escalation.
Jamie (oncall): All proxies now with retry patch. Observability shows successful reductions in client-facing errors.
Cloudflare Support Bot: Confirmed rollback resolved edge routing flap. No further action required from vendor side.
Alex M.: Starting to roll back temporary origin-reroute to avoid sustained origin load. Will step down from 5% -> 1% -> 0% over 10 minutes.
SRE Lead: Monitor closely during rollback. If errors increase, reenable.
Infra Bot: Automated smoke tests post-rollback: all passing for NA/EU. APAC minor blips — continue monitoring.
Support: Sent customer update: "Issue largely mitigated; Cloudflare has applied a fix. We're monitoring and will post a postmortem in 24 hours. Contact support if you see continued issues"
Priya K.: Filing postmortem ticket and assigning owners. Drafting timeline and RCA to include Cloudflare routing flap, our mitigation choices, and recommended product-level resiliency improvements (multi-CDN, client retry policy, region-aware SDK).
Jamie (oncall): Leaving on-call note and handoff to next shift — incident suppressed, but still under watch. Handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/oncall/handoffs/2519001234.
SRE Lead: Thanks team. Final checklist: verify artifacts uploaded, customer comms sent, postmortem scheduled. Close incident when postmortem live. :white_check_mark:
